findings.heading: Syntax
findings.proposition: The Russian edge-attribute list glosses `fontcolor` as "(ширина стрелки)" = "(width of arrow)"; the English gives `fontcolor` no gloss at all and attaches "(width of arrow)" to a different attribute.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader who wants to change the thickness of an edge sets `fontcolor`, which sets the label text colour instead. The arrow keeps its default width and the label silently changes colour, with no error to explain it.

findings.heading: Syntax
findings.proposition: The English lists `penwidth` as an editable edge attribute controlling arrow width; the Russian edge-attribute list contains no `penwidth` entry (it runs `fontname`, `fontsize`, `fontcolor`, `minlen`).
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader concludes DiagrammeR offers no way to set edge line thickness and cannot find the attribute name, even though `penwidth` works and is documented one list higher for nodes.

findings.heading: Plotting from dataset
findings.proposition: The Russian prose states the `hospital` and `age_cat` columns are renamed to `источник` and `цель`; the code chunk immediately below renames them to `source` and `target`, and every later step (`links$source`, `Source = "IDsource"`) depends on the English names.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader following the prose writes `rename(источник = hospital, цель = age_cat)`, and the next chunk fails at `match(links$source, ...)` because no column `source` exists.

findings.heading: Load packages (Alluvial/Sankey Diagrams)
findings.proposition: The English sends the reader to the R basics page with a working link target (`[R basics](basics.qmd)`); the Russian writes `[Основы R]` with no link target at all, so the cross-reference carries no destination.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader who wants the background on R packages sees plain bracketed text that does not navigate anywhere and has no page filename to search for. The identical sentence earlier in the same chapter (line 31) does link correctly, so the reader cannot tell the omission is an error.

findings.heading: Import data
findings.proposition: The English makes loading the linelist conditional ("If you want to follow along for this part, load it directly with ..."); the Russian drops the condition and issues the load as an unconditional instruction ("Загрузите их напрямую с помощью ...").
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader who only wants the flow-diagram sections believes the dataset download is required for the chapter, and downloads it needlessly rather than skipping to the sections that need no data.
